shared_elements: tall upright slab/monolith with rounded top
incised/low-relief carving on a flat frontal surface
roughly bilateral symmetry about a central axis
small repeated linear/glyph-like marks in the upper zone
justification: Both are tall, round-topped monolithic surfaces organised symmetrically into stacked zones, each containing a prominent circular disc and clusters of small incised sign-like marks near the top, which gives a comparable silhouette at a glance. Beyond that the correspondence collapses: A is a precise pen drawing dominated by dense rows of tiny script and slender profile figures beneath a rayed disc, while B is a weathered three-dimensional boulder-like carving with a few large, blunt, frontal shapes and no script-like registers.
